XIX.}}</noinclude>that vvhich thou didst not sovv. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=22}}† He saith to him, By thine ovvne mouth I iudge thee, naughtie seruant. Thou didst knovv that I am an austere man, taking vp that I set not dovvne, and reaping that vvhich I sovved not: {{verse|chapter=19|verse=23}}† and vvhy didst thou not giue my money to the banke, and I comming might certes vvith vsurie haue exacted it? {{verse|chapter=19|verse=24}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ See annotations Matth. 25, 29, &c.}}∷ And he said to them that stoode by, Take the pound avvay from him, and giue it to him that hath the ten poundes. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=25}}† And they said to him, Lord, he hath ten poundes. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=26}}† But I say to you, that to euery one that hath shal be giuen: and from him that hath not, that also vvhich he hath shal be taken from him.⊣ {{verse|chapter=19|verse=27}}† But as for those mine enemies that vvould not haue me reigne ouer them, bring them hither: and kil them before me.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=28}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ THE fifth part of the Gospel, Of the Holy weeke of his Passion in Hierusalem.}}∷ And hauing said these things, he vvent before ascending to Hierusalem. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=29}}† And it came to passe {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 21, 1. Mr. 11, 1. Io. 12, 1. 15.''}}* vvhen he vvas come nigh to Bethphagé and Bethania vnto the mount called Oliuet, he sent tvvo of his Disciples, {{verse|chapter=19|verse=30}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ PALME SVNDAY.}}∷ saying, Goe into the tovvne vvhich is ouer against, into the vvhich as you enter, you shal finde the colt of an asse tied, on vvhich no man euer hath sitten: loose him, and bring him. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=31}}† And if any man aske you, VVhy loose you him? You shal say thus to him, because our Lord needeth his seruice. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=32}}† And they that vvere sent, vvent their vvaies, and found as he said to them, the colt standing. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=33}}† And vvhen they loosed the colt, the ovvners thereof said to them, VVhy loose you the colt? {{verse|chapter=19|verse=34}}† But they said, because our Lord hath neede of him. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=35}}† And they brought him to {{sc|Iesvs}}. And casting their garments vpon the colt, they set {{sc|Iesvs}} therevpon. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=36}}† And as he vvent, they spred their garments vnderneath in the vvay. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=37}}† And vvhen he approched novv to the descent of mount-Oliuet, al the multitudes of {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`his disciples'',}}`them that descended', began vvith ioy to praise God vvith a loude voice, for al the miracles that they had seen, {{verse|chapter=19|verse=38}}† saying, Blessed is he that commeth king in the name of our Lord, peace in heauen, and glorie on high. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=39}}† And certaine Pharisees of the multitudes said to him, Maister, rebuke thy disciples. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=40}}† To vvhom he said, I say to you, That if these hold their peace, the stones shal crie. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=41}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpon the 9. Sunday after Pentecost.}}And as he drevv neere, seeing the citie, he vvept vpon it, saying, {{verse|chapter=19|verse=42}}† Because if thou also hadst knovven, and that in this thy day, the things that pertaine to thy peace: but novv they are hid from thine<noinclude>{{rh|||eies.}}</noinclude>
